findings.rationale: normalize() rewrites enum member comparisons via raw substring replacement (output.replace on the pattern variable == member and the != variant). The pattern matches inside longer identifiers: comparing an enum-typed variable to a non-member token that extends a member (e.g. s == opened when only open is declared) is silently rewritten to the mangled member, and which rewrite wins depends on member declaration order. The word-boundary-aware replace_identifier() used for state fields is not applied here, so generated code semantics can change without any error.

safe() maps every non-alphanumeric character to underscore and lower_name() folds case, so distinct domain names collapse to identical generated identifiers (fields a-b and a_b both yield a_b; aggregates Foo and foo both yield the state prefix foo_ via state_name). No collision detection is visible in the admitted excerpt, so lowered output can contain duplicate or aliased symbols.

normalize() applies whole-string textual rewrites (&& to and, || to or, -> to =>) and then replaces state field names across the entire rendered expression without tokenization, so occurrences inside string literals are also rewritten. The admitted excerpt truncates at line 400, mid replace_identifier call, so the replacement target is not visible; the substitution scope nonetheless spans the full expression text.
